gaps.title: needs_changes re-submit (fix route) reaches pending_review but creates NO verification_case → counted on dashboard, invisible/unopenable in queue
gaps.detail: admin_reject_verification with outcome='needs_changes' CLOSES the case (verification_cases.state='closed') and sets users.verification_status='needs_changes' (20260627100400_admin_case_rpcs.sql:286-298). The user then re-submits via /api/onboarding/fix, which transitions verification_status back to 'pending_review' (fix/route.ts:58-63) but performs NO verification_cases insert — unlike selfie/route.ts:73-85 which has the idempotent case-creation block. Result: the user is now counted by the dashboard 'Заявки на проверке' card (admin/page.tsx:29-31 counts users.verification_status='pending_review') but has ZERO open cases. loadMyQueue (load-queue.ts:90-99, state<>'closed') and loadUnassignedQueue (load-queue.ts:102-112, state='new') both read verification_cases, so the user appears in NEITHER queue and there is no /admin/cases/[id] row to open. Operator sees 'нужно верифицировать' (count > 0, accent border) but the queue is empty and the user is permanently stuck in pending_review with no way for a moderator to action them. This is the primary live bug and it triggers on the completely normal needs_changes → re-upload cycle.
gaps.fix_hint: Enforce the invariant verification_status='pending_review' ⟺ exactly one open verification_case (state<>'closed'). Preferred single-source fix: an AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on users WHEN new.verification_status='pending_review' that inserts a state='new' case if none open exists — atomic and covers every path (transition_user writes users.verification_status via a plain UPDATE, and admin_unblock_verification does a direct UPDATE, so a table trigger catches all of them). App-level alternative: extract the selfie/route.ts:73-85 idempotent block into ensureOpenVerificationCase(userId) and call it from fix/route.ts and the unblock RPC — but note this is the same scattered pattern that produced the bug.

gaps.title: Superadmin unblock-verification RPC returns user to pending_review but creates NO verification_case
gaps.detail: The current admin_unblock_verification (latest def: 20260620920000_split_window_and_jti_fixes.sql:100-149, 3-arg signature matching the route call at unblock-verification/route.ts:38-42) sets users.verification_status='pending_review' and onboarding_step='moderation_pending' (lines 145-149) but does NOT insert a verification_case. After a superadmin revokes a blocking-reject, the user is counted by the dashboard but again has no open case → invisible/unopenable in the new queue/case studio. Same divergence class as VF-1, on the incident-response/misclick path. (Note: the route.ts comment references a legacy 4-arg p_phone_hash version, but the highest-timestamp migration redefines it to the 3-arg form the route actually calls, so this path is live, not latent behind a signature error.)
gaps.fix_hint: Covered automatically by the AFTER UPDATE trigger on users in the VF-1 fix (the RPC's UPDATE users SET verification_status='pending_review' would fire it). If choosing the app-level approach instead, add an ensureOpenVerificationCase(userId) insert inside the admin_unblock_verification RPC after the users UPDATE.

gaps.title: Dashboard counter and queue use different sources of truth (users.verification_status vs verification_cases)
gaps.detail: The 'Заявки на проверке' StatCard counts users where verification_status='pending_review' (admin/page.tsx:29-31, no lifecycle filter, links to /admin/queue/mine) while the destination queue lists open verification_cases only (load-queue.ts:95 state<>'closed' for mine; load-queue.ts:108 state='new' for unassigned). These two populations only coincide when the pending_review⟺open-case invariant holds — which VF-1/VF-2 break. Even structurally the counter can never equal the visible queue: a case in state assigned/in_review/data_entry/ready_to_decide with no assignee-match will not show in loadMyQueue for a given admin, and only state='new' shows in unassigned. The counter is a per-user count; the queue is a per-case, per-assignee view. Any non-zero mismatch presents to the operator as phantom work.
gaps.fix_hint: After enforcing the invariant, make the dashboard count read the same source as the queue: count verification_cases where state<>'closed' (matching loadMyQueue's predicate), not users.verification_status. This keeps the headline number consistent with what's actually openable. Counting only state='new' would undercount claimed-but-open cases.

gaps.title: Guard predicate (pending_review AND lifecycle_state='onboarding') is a third, stricter definition of 'in queue' — and the new case studio bypasses it entirely
gaps.detail: checkInQueueOrSuperPage / requireInQueueOrSuper define 'in the moderation queue' as verification_status='pending_review' AND lifecycle_state='onboarding' (guard.ts:328 and guard.ts:370) — stricter than both the counter (VF-3) and the case-based queue. This is a fourth divergent predicate on the counter/queue/guard/case-existence axis. Compounding it: the primary new flow /admin/cases/[id] (cases/[id]/page.tsx:16-19) calls only requireAdmin() and scopes access by case assignee_id inside CaseStudio (CaseStudio.tsx:90) — it NEVER calls checkInQueueOrSuperPage. So a moderator's data-scope for the main verification flow is governed by case assignment, while the guard's stricter user-column predicate only governs the legacy /admin/verifications and /admin/users pages. The two scoping models can disagree (e.g. a user in pending_review with lifecycle_state != 'onboarding' would pass case-based access but be hidden by the guard), and the guard predicate can diverge from case existence in either direction.
gaps.fix_hint: Pick one source of truth for 'is this user actionable by a moderator' and reuse it in the guard. Once cases are the source of truth (VF-1), express in-scope as 'user has an open verification_case assigned to this admin (or unassigned+new)', so the guard's legacy-page check matches the case studio's assignment-based access rather than re-deriving from user columns.

gaps.title: Only two code paths ever create a verification_case; every other path into pending_review depends on a pre-existing open case
gaps.detail: Enumerated case-creation sites: (1) one-time backfill in 20260627100100_verification_cases.sql:85-92 (only for users already pending_review at migration time, idempotent via NOT EXISTS open case); (2) selfie/route.ts:80-84 (idempotent guard on any non-closed case for the user). No DB trigger auto-creates cases (confirmed: no 'insert into verification_cases' anywhere in migrations except the backfill; user_identity only references the table via FK). Paths that set verification_status='pending_review' WITHOUT creating a case: fix/route.ts:58 (VF-1) and admin_unblock_verification (VF-2). Additionally, selfie/route.ts's idempotency guard (neq state 'closed') means a re-submission after needs_changes finds the prior case ALREADY closed, so even the selfie path would fail to create a fresh case on that cycle — but needs_changes re-entry goes through fix/route.ts (per state machine types.ts:108 needs_changes→moderation_pending / doc_upload / selfie_upload), not selfie/route.ts, so the missing-case gap lands squarely on fix. This inventory shows the invariant is maintained by scattered ad-hoc inserts rather than a single enforced rule.
gaps.fix_hint: Consolidate case creation into one enforced mechanism (the AFTER UPDATE trigger from VF-1). Removing the responsibility from selfie/route.ts and fix/route.ts and centralizing it in the DB guarantees no future pending_review path can regress the invariant.

gaps.title: No hard-DELETE operator action for test/spam accounts (only soft erase_user exists)
gaps.detail: There is no admin route or RPC to hard-remove a user across all tables. Confirmed by grep: no admin delete/reset/hard_delete route in src/app/api/admin/ and no reset/purge/hard_delete RPC in supabase/migrations/. The only deletion path is the SOFT, GDPR/erasure-oriented erase_user RPC (supabase/migrations/20260620920000_split_window_and_jti_fixes.sql:35), invoked ONLY by the USER-facing endpoint /api/account?action=delete (src/app/api/account/route.ts:87). erase_user is wrong for a test/spam hard-delete for three reasons: (1) it KEEPS the users row as a tombstone (sets deleted_at + lifecycle_state='deleted', nulls telegram_id/phone) rather than removing it (lines 77-87); (2) it INSERTS document_sha_blacklist rows for passport/selfie SHAs (lines 42-52) and the /api/account caller also inserts a 90-day phone_blacklist tombstone (route.ts:64-73) — poisoning the anti-catfish blacklist with junk test SHAs/phones, which is actively harmful for a throwaway account; (3) it does NOT touch several child tables that reference users. A true hard delete via `DELETE FROM users WHERE id=$1` is SAFE and cascades cleanly: I grepped every migration for FKs to users(id) and ALL child tables are `on delete cascade` (consents, user_documents, user_profiles, profile_photos, otp_codes, quiz_answers, quiz_results, match_requests, match_views, chats, chat_messages, daily_request_quotas, user_state_transitions, reports, blocks — init_schema.sql:56-256; tg_outbox 20260625000000:36; start_token_uses 20260620920000:198; user_identity 20260627100200:10; verification_cases+case_events+case_notes 20260627100100:24,42,63). The ONLY non-cascade FKs are document_sha_blacklist.source_user_id and phone_blacklist.linked_user_id, both `on delete set null` (20260620300000:28, 20260620500000:15) — so a raw DELETE will NOT fail on any restrict/no-action FK, and correctly leaves anti-abuse tombstones intact if any exist. NOTE case_events/case_notes have an append-only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger (20260627100100:52-58) that raises on direct delete, but the FK cascade from verification_cases bypasses row-level triggers only if... actually the trigger fires on cascade deletes too, so the delete must remove verification_cases rows in a way the trigger allows OR the cascade will raise — this must be validated (drop case_events rows are protected). admin_audit_log.entity_id is plain text, not an FK (init_schema.sql:225-240), so the audit record survives the row deletion.
gaps.fix_hint: Add POST /api/admin/users/[id]/delete (new route.ts) following the ban/unban superadmin pattern. Gate superadmin-only exactly like unban/route.ts:16-17 (session.role!=='superadmin' -> 403). Require a typed confirmation body (e.g. {confirm:'DELETE', reason} with reason.length>=3) plus expected_updated_at optimistic-concurrency guard (as decision/route.ts:29). Implement a dedicated admin_hard_delete_user(p_user_id, p_admin_id) PL/pgSQL RPC (security invoker, single transaction) that: collects profile_photos.path + docs-bucket paths BEFORE deletion (mirror account/route.ts:75-99 storage cleanup), deletes verification_cases rows for the user FIRST (so case_events/case_notes cascade before the append-only DELETE trigger blocks — validate this trigger interaction; may need to temporarily use a SECURITY DEFINER function or session_replication_role), then `DELETE FROM users WHERE id=p_user_id` letting all cascade FKs fire. Do NOT insert document_sha_blacklist or phone_blacklist tombstones (unlike erase_user/account.delete) — this is a throwaway account. Storage removal is best-effort post-transaction (BUCKET_PHOTOS/BUCKET_DOCUMENTS, see account/route.ts:6,96-99). Write adminAudit({action:'hard_delete_user', entity:'user', entityId:id, reason, ip:trustedIp(req)}) — guard.ts:40 — BEFORE the row disappears (entity_id survives as text). Confirmation dialog in UI via Dialog + danger styling (DecisionPanel.tsx pattern).

gaps.title: No RESTART-onboarding operator action (reset user to redo onboarding from scratch)
gaps.detail: There is no route or RPC to reset a user so they re-run onboarding. Requested reset per the onboarding_step enum (init_schema.sql:7): onboarding_step='language', verification_status='not_started', profile_completion='not_started', quiz_completion='not_started', lifecycle_state='onboarding'; wipe user_profiles, profile_photos, quiz_answers, quiz_results, user_documents, user_identity, verification_cases (+cascading case_events/case_notes); KEEP the users row + telegram_id (identity anchor) so the same TG account resumes. Two correctness traps confirmed against code: (1) This CANNOT be implemented with the existing tryTransition/transition helper. transition() (src/lib/state-machine/transitions.ts:59-66) validates onboarding_step against ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS, which is a FORWARD-only graph (types-v3.test.ts asserts profile_basic->profile_appearance->... forward edges only). Sending onboarding_step backward from 'active'/'profile_*' to 'language' will throw TransitionError -> tryTransition returns {ok:false,error:'wrong_step'} (transitions.ts:99). So a backward reset needs a dedicated RPC that bypasses the forward-only guard, not tryTransition. (2) The reset must NOT insert document_sha_blacklist/phone_blacklist tombstones — if it reuses erase_user or blocking-reject logic, the user's own passport/phone SHA lands on the blacklist and they can't re-verify with their own document during the redo (the onboarding document upload path already checks these tombstones — see src/app/api/onboarding/document/route.ts:25 comment on SHA-tombstone from blocking-reject/erase_user). (3) consents (init_schema.sql:54, stores ip/user_agent/accepted_at as legal records) — wiping them forces re-consent but destroys the prior legal record; KEEP-vs-WIPE is a policy decision to surface, not silently wipe. Spec distinction: chat7_admin.txt lists request_re_verification (a SOFTER redo-verification-only action) as a moderator capability — do NOT conflate it with full RESTART, which wipes profile+quiz+identity too.
gaps.fix_hint: Add POST /api/admin/users/[id]/restart-onboarding, superadmin-only (unban/route.ts:16-17 pattern), with confirmation + reason + expected_updated_at guard. Back it with a dedicated admin_restart_onboarding(p_user_id, p_admin_id, p_wipe_consents boolean) PL/pgSQL RPC in a single transaction that: DELETEs verification_cases (cascades case_events/case_notes — mind the append-only trigger, 20260627100100:52), user_identity, user_documents, user_profiles, profile_photos, quiz_answers, quiz_results (optionally consents per p_wipe_consents); UPDATEs users SET onboarding_step='language', verification_status='not_started', profile_completion='not_started', quiz_completion='not_started', lifecycle_state='onboarding', sanction_level='none', paused_at/blocked_at/blocked_reason=null, keeping telegram_id and (decide) phone_verified; and INSERTs a user_state_transitions row (mirror erase_user's manual insert, 20260620920000:89-93) since it bypasses the transition helper. Do NOT write any *_blacklist tombstone. Best-effort storage cleanup for photo/doc buckets afterward (account/route.ts:95-99). adminAudit({action:'restart_onboarding', entity:'user', ...}) per guard.ts:40. Guard against restarting a 'blocked'/'pending_ban' user (return 409) so it can't be used to launder a ban.

gaps.title: Client detail page has no user-level action UI surface — button placement is itself missing
gaps.detail: Even the EXISTING user-level operator actions (ban/unban/unblock-verification) have NO UI: grep across src/ found zero client-side callers of /api/admin/users/[id]/ban|unban|unblock-verification (only case blocking-reject is wired, via DecisionPanel.tsx:57). ModerationTab.tsx (the natural home) is entirely read-only — it lists verification_cases and reports with no action buttons (src/app/admin/clients/[id]/ModerationTab.tsx, whole file). ClientHero.tsx renders only status pills + copy buttons, no actions. ClientTabs.tsx has tabs [identity, profile, photos, activity, moderation] with no danger-zone. So 'where the DELETE / RESTART buttons go' has no existing surface to attach to and must be built. Spec confirms these are legitimate superadmin single-account actions when confirmed+audited: chat7_admin.txt forbids only BULK delete (line 2617 'нельзя массово ... удалить аккаунты') and forbids LOWER roles from 'удалять аккаунт' (line 9058, Support cannot delete), has a 'Удалённые' user-status filter (line 2537), and section 2.2 requires audit-logging of 'удаление данных' (line 9864). There is NO explicit single-user 'delete account' or 'restart onboarding' action defined anywhere in chat7 — they are spec-CONSISTENT but not spec-SPECIFIED.
gaps.fix_hint: Convert ModerationTab.tsx into (or add below it) a client-component 'Danger zone' section, or add the actions to ClientHero, following the DecisionPanel.tsx pattern: 'use client' + Button (@/components/admin-ops/Button) + Dialog (@/components/admin-ops/Dialog) for confirmation, fetch POST to the new endpoints, router.refresh() on success, inline error display (DecisionPanel.tsx:1-90). Gate the buttons' visibility on session.role==='superadmin' (page.tsx already has session.role available, passed to OpsShell at page.tsx:68). Require typed confirmation for DELETE (irreversible) mirroring the blocking-reject confirm dialog (DecisionPanel.tsx:283 '⛔ ... необратимо'). While here, also wire the already-existing ban/unban/unblock-verification endpoints into this same danger-zone, since they are currently API-only and unreachable from the UI.

gaps.title: How the two systems differ + options A (align shared primitives) vs B (adopt editorial) — decision, not a defect
gaps.detail:
The admin was intentionally built as a separate operator tool and IS visually coherent within itself; a full re-skin is a DECISION, not an assumed fix. Concrete differences across four axes:

PALETTE — Admin: warm off-white surfaces (--admin-bg #fafaf8 / surface #ffffff / surface-2 #f4f3ef, globals.css:127-129) with a deep slate-blue accent (--admin-accent #2d4a5c, globals.css:138; admin-tokens.ts:17) used for primary buttons, active nav, tab underlines, stepper. Mini-app editorial: paper off-white (--color-v2-paper #faf6f1, globals.css:33) but its PRIMARY CTA is near-black ink #0a0908 on paper (v2/Button.tsx:41-43, --color-v2-ink-100 globals.css:36), NOT an accent color. The nominal v2 accent is amethyst #4a2c5a (globals.css:43) but it is barely used as a primary surface; coral #e2526b is V1 legacy still live only in WelcomeBranded.tsx (globals.css:8, WelcomeBranded.tsx:167). Net contrast: admin = slate-blue-on-warm-neutral; mini-app = near-black-ink-on-paper. (The brief's 'coral accent' is V1 legacy, not the current editorial primary.)

TYPE — Admin: Inter sans everywhere, 13px base, no serif by design; JetBrains Mono for PINFL/passport (globals.css:147-149,161). Mini-app: editorial serif headlines are the hero visual (--font-v2-display Druk/Kazimir, Headline.tsx:38, globals.css:99-109) over Inter body; larger scale (44/32/24px, Headline.tsx:19-24) vs admin's 11-15px. NOTE both systems name webfonts that are never actually loaded (see D6).

DENSITY — Admin: compact, table-driven, 36px rows (globals.css:151), 28-32px buttons (Button.tsx:53), tight 8-12px cell padding (ClientsTable.tsx). Mini-app: 'one object per screen', max-width 420px, generous 24-32px padding, centered (MiniAppShell.tsx:44-51), 16px full-width buttons (v2/Button.tsx:30-32).

COMPONENTS — the two systems DUPLICATE rather than SHARE primitives: two separate Button implementations (admin-ops/Button.tsx vs v2/Button.tsx) with different variants/sizes; two token delivery mechanisms — admin uses a TS object (ADMIN.* from admin-tokens.ts, consumed as inline JS) while v2 uses CSS custom properties (var(--color-v2-*)). There is no shared primitive layer.

OPTIONS:
(A) Keep the ops-tool identity (Linear/Salesforce vibe, per the 2026-06-27 design decision at globals.css:119-125) but polish: fix the token/inconsistency items D1-D6 below, and reconcile the two parallel token systems (unify delivery so admin-tokens.ts mirrors CSS vars rather than diverging). Lower effort, preserves intentional separation.
(B) Adopt the editorial look in admin (serif headlines, paper palette, amethyst/ink accent, low density). High effort, works against the deliberate operator-tool ergonomics (dense tables want sans + tight rows), and would fight the existing 'no serifs in data tables' principle (globals.css:124). Recommend NOT doing B wholesale; if any editorial borrowing is wanted, limit it to the login/dashboard chrome, not data screens.

This entry is the palette/type/density/component comparison and the A/B enumeration; it is a decision to raise with the founder, not a bug.

gaps.title: Editorial serif leaks into the admin logo — cross-DNA bleed against the 'no serifs' ops decision
gaps.detail: OpsSidebar renders the 'Baxtlilar Ops' wordmark with fontFamily: 'var(--font-v2-display)' — the mini-app's editorial display serif (Druk/Kazimir/Georgia) — inside a tool whose design decision explicitly states 'никаких серифов' / no serifs (globals.css:124). This is the single clearest place where the two design DNAs collide: an editorial serif logo sitting atop an otherwise all-Inter operator sidebar. It also couples the admin bundle to a v2 token. If the ops identity is kept (option A), this should be Inter (or a deliberately-chosen ops wordmark font), not the editorial serif.

gaps.title: Border-radii are hardcoded and inconsistent; the --admin-radius tokens are never consumed
gaps.detail: globals.css:155-156 defines --admin-radius:6px and --admin-radius-lg:8px, and admin-tokens.ts is meant to mirror the token system, but NO component reads them — every radius is a raw literal. Values are inconsistent even for the same class of surface: cards/tables/dialogs/drawers use 8 (ClientsTable.tsx:43, Dialog.tsx:59, PhotosTable.tsx:47, DecisionPanel.tsx:120), buttons/search/topbar use 6 (Button.tsx:66, SearchBar.tsx:48, OpsTopBar.tsx:32), pills/inputs/textareas use 4 (StatusPill.tsx:39, ReasonPicker.tsx:24,51, DecisionPanel.tsx:350), and the login card uses 10 (login/page.tsx:65) — a one-off that matches nothing else. The 10px login card next to 8px dialogs reads as unfinished. Fix: route all radii through --admin-radius/--admin-radius-lg (add a card token if 8 is intended) and drop the 10px outlier.

gaps.title: Density modes are advertised in tokens/comment but not implemented — no consumer, no data-density switch
gaps.detail: globals.css:151-153 defines three row-height tokens (--admin-row-h 36px, --admin-row-h-cosy 28px, --admin-row-h-comfortable 44px) and the block comment at globals.css:123 sells 'density modes' as a feature of the ops tool. Grep shows zero consumers: no component reads any --admin-row-h token, tables hardcode padding (ClientsTable.tsx:66,97 etc.), and there is no data-density attribute or density toggle anywhere. This is a half-built feature — either wire the density switch (OpsShell could set data-density and tables read the row-h var) or remove the unused tokens and the 'density modes' claim from the comment so the token file reflects reality.

gaps.title: Dead admin tokens: borderStrong and the .pinfl/.passport-num/.mono utility classes are never used
gaps.detail: --admin-border-strong (#c9c5bb, globals.css:130; borderStrong in admin-tokens.ts:10) is defined but never referenced — all borders use the lighter --admin-border. The mono utility classes .pinfl/.passport-num/.mono (globals.css:165-171) are also unused: components instead inline fontFamily: ADMIN.fontMono directly (CaseHeader.tsx:48, ClientsTable.tsx:109,138, DecisionPanel.tsx:148). This is drift between the declared token/utility surface and actual usage; prune the dead tokens/classes or adopt them, so the system is a source of truth rather than aspirational.

gaps.title: Admin body paints a third neutral (Tailwind slate) that neither token system uses — latent but inconsistent
gaps.detail: The admin root layout body is bg-slate-100 text-slate-800 (cool Tailwind slate), which is a THIRD neutral palette distinct from both the admin token bg (--admin-bg #fafaf8 warm off-white) and v2 paper (#faf6f1). In practice this is mostly LATENT: OpsShell sets data-ops='true' which repaints to --admin-bg (globals.css:158), and the login page paints ADMIN.bg over its <main> (login/page.tsx:52), so the slate only shows during cold paint / on any admin surface not wrapped by those. Still, it's a stray cool-gray that contradicts the warm-neutral ops palette and should be set to --admin-bg (or the admin token) at the body level to avoid a cold flash and keep one source of truth.

gaps.title: Named webfonts are not loaded in either system — tokens promise fonts that fall back to system/serif defaults
gaps.detail: Neither design system actually loads the fonts its tokens name. Admin: app/admin/layout.tsx loads no font and sets no font className, so --admin-font-sans 'Inter' and --admin-font-mono 'JetBrains Mono' (globals.css:147-149) fall back to system sans / -apple-system and Menlo. Mini-app: the root at app/[locale]/layout.tsx:11-12 loads Geist + Geist_Mono via next/font (as --font-geist-sans/--font-geist-mono), but the v2 tokens reference 'Inter' (--font-v2-body) and 'JetBrains Mono' (--font-v2-mono, globals.css:57-60) — which are never loaded, so v2 body/mono also fall back rather than rendering the named fonts. Most consequential: the editorial DISPLAY serif (Druk Cyrillic / Kazimir), the concept's hero visual, is marked 'будет лицензировано' / to-be-licensed (globals.css:53-55) and has no @font-face — so every v2 headline currently renders in Georgia/Times, not the intended serif. Effect on this comparison: the type contrast the brief describes is partly aspirational today; both admin and mini-app render in fallback faces. Decide per-system: either load the named fonts (next/font or @font-face) or update the tokens to the fonts actually shipped (e.g. Geist for the mini-app).

gaps.title: RBAC reduced to 2 hardcoded roles vs spec's role matrix (Identity/Photo/Profile/Safety/Support/Finance/Analyst + custom)
gaps.detail: not_yet_built. Spec Screen 21 (l.15009+) and the RBAC section (l.1789) require a StaffRole/Permission matrix with distinct roles: Super Admin, Admin, Moderator, Photo Moderator, Identity Manager, Support, Safety Manager, Finance, Analyst, International/Individual Manager (spec cites 18 roles, systemic + custom + read-only). Built system has ONLY two roles hardcoded at the DB check constraint: role in ('superadmin','moderator') (admin_users, 20260531000000_init_schema.sql:221) and mirrored in the type union (src/lib/admin/session.ts:10, src/lib/admin/guard.ts:11). All gating is a binary superOnly flag (src/components/admin-ops/OpsSidebar.tsx:38-51) or session.role !== 'superadmin' checks (e.g. src/app/admin/reports/page.tsx:65, decision route:22). There is no per-permission model, no separate document-view / download / sensitive-access permissions the spec repeatedly mandates (Screen 5 l.4408 'view_identity_document', 'download_identity_document'; Screen 10 l.7293 'open_chat_for_complaint_review'). Operationally this means the platform cannot restrict, e.g., a Photo Moderator from seeing passport PII, or a Support agent from acting on complaints — the spec's core 'minimally necessary privilege' promise (l.136, l.15037) is unenforceable with 2 roles.
gaps.fix_hint: Introduce staff_roles + permissions tables and a role-permission matrix; replace the 2-value role check with a permission-based guard. Minimum operational subset: Identity Manager, Photo Moderator, Safety Manager, Support, Finance, Analyst, Admin, Super Admin. Gate document view/download and complaint-chat access behind discrete permissions with requires_reason + audit.

gaps.title: No Staff & Roles management screen (add/invite/change-role/block staff, invitations, last-activity)
gaps.detail: not_yet_built. Spec Screen 21 (l.15009-16005) requires a full staff-management module: list all admins with status/role/department/last_activity/has_2fa, add/invite staff (invite_staff_member), resend invitation, change_role (requires reason+comment+confirmation+audit; extra confirmation for Super Admin), change_department, grant/revoke sensitive access, block/unblock staff with session termination, reset password, require 2FA, staff audit log, export. None of this exists: there is no /admin/staff or /admin/employees page (src/app/admin/* contains only analytics, audit, cases, clients, login, photos, queue, reports, users, verifications) and no staff API routes (src/app/api/admin/* has no staff/roles endpoints). admin_users has no status, department, last_activity, or invitation columns (20260531000000_init_schema.sql:218-224). Admins today can only be created by direct DB insert. Operationally: no way to onboard/offboard a moderator, revoke a departed employee's access, or audit who has sensitive access.
gaps.fix_hint: Build /admin/staff screen + StaffMember/StaffInvitation entities and CRUD API; add status (active/inactive/blocked/invited), last_activity_at, department, invite flow, and session-termination on block. Enforce change-role guardrails (reason/comment/confirm/audit) per spec l.15900.

gaps.title: No 2FA / SSO for staff — password-only login
gaps.detail: not_yet_built. Spec repeatedly mandates 2FA for staff: Screen 22 security KPI 'есть ли сотрудники без 2FA' (l.16xxx), Screen 21 filter has_2fa + requires_2fa on invite and sensitive-access (l.15900+ conditions require_2fa:true), enterprise-checklist l.1812 '2FA / SSO для сотрудников', l.2024, audit action admin_staff_2fa_requested. Built login is single-factor password only: src/app/api/admin/login/route.ts verifies password (line 35) then immediately setAdminSession (line 61) with no second factor. admin_users has no 2fa_secret / totp columns (20260531000000_init_schema.sql:218-224). Session is an 8h HMAC cookie (src/lib/admin/session.ts:8) with no step-up. Operationally: a leaked admin password fully compromises the moderation console, including passport PII and ban powers.
gaps.fix_hint: Add TOTP 2FA: store per-admin secret, enforce a verify step between password check and setAdminSession, and expose a 'без 2FA' security indicator. Make 2FA mandatory for roles with sensitive access.

gaps.title: Dashboard has no SLA / queue-capacity / 'Требуют внимания' work table
gaps.detail: not_yet_built (partial infra only). Spec Screen 1 (l.2107-2445) requires the dashboard to surface SLA breaches and queue load: KPIs incl. critical_complaints, moderation_queues with current/capacity, trust_status (verified share, average_moderation_time, matching_enabled), a gender_balance imbalance signal, and a 'Требуют внимания' table with per-case created_at/assigned_at/due_at/priority/sla_status/responsible_employee, with overdue rows visually flagged (l.2278, l.2433). Built dashboard (src/app/admin/page.tsx:59-103) shows only flat counts (pending review, photos, open reports, population, demographics) as StatCards — no SLA, no due_at, no priority, no capacity, no 'requires attention' queue, no average moderation time. SLA infra is minimal: only a 7-day stale-case reclaim RPC exists (supabase/migrations/20260630010000_verification_case_sla.sql:12) invoked from cron; there is no per-case due_at/priority column or SLA status computed anywhere. Operationally the team cannot see which cases/complaints are overdue — the spec's stated purpose 'не проспать пожар' (l.2278) is unmet.
gaps.fix_hint: Add due_at + priority + assigned_at to verification_cases and reports; compute sla_status; build a 'Требуют внимания' table on the dashboard with overdue highlighting and queue current/capacity gauges; surface average_moderation_time and verified-share trust KPIs.

gaps.title: Complaint handling missing spec actions: no assignment, priority, evidence, related-chat, restriction, escalate-to-legal, notes; no complaint detail card
gaps.detail: broken/incomplete vs spec. Spec Screen 9-10 (l.6284, l.6926-7360) require a complaint detail card with participants, description, evidence list (safety_only), related_chat (permission+reason gated), priority/category, assigned_to, and 8 actions: assign_moderator, send_to_safety, request_clarification, apply_restriction, block_user, close_complaint, escalate_to_legal, add_moderator_note (l.7293). Built reports handling is a flat superadmin-only list (src/app/admin/reports/page.tsx) with an inline ReportActions component exposing only 3 status transitions — in_progress/action_taken/not_confirmed (src/components/admin/report-actions.tsx:12-15); the decision route (src/app/api/admin/reports/[id]/decision/route.ts:10) allows in_progress/action_taken/not_confirmed/escalated/closed status only — no assignment, no evidence viewing, no related-chat access, no restriction application, no legal escalation, no moderator notes. The reports table itself lacks priority, assigned_to, category, and evidence columns (20260531000000_init_schema.sql:241-251). There is no per-complaint detail route (/admin/reports/[id] does not exist). Operationally the safety team cannot triage by priority, assign owners, review evidence, or escalate.
gaps.fix_hint: Add priority/category/assigned_to/evidence to reports; build /admin/reports/[id] detail card; implement assign, request-clarification, apply-restriction, escalate-to-legal, add-note actions with permission+reason+audit; gate evidence and related-chat behind Safety permissions.

gaps.title: No Blocks & Restrictions screen; ban/unban API exists but is not wired into any UI
gaps.detail: broken. Spec Screen 11 (l.7441) requires a Blocks-and-restrictions module (apply/lift restrictions and bans, limits, with reasons and audit). In the built app the F-119 two-person ban dispatcher exists server-side (src/lib/admin/guard.ts:135 dispatchBanAction; routes src/app/api/admin/users/[id]/ban/route.ts and /unban) but NO admin UI calls it: a grep for ban/unban fetch across src/app and src/components finds only unblock-verification wired. The old UserActions ban button was removed and /admin/users now just redirects to /admin/clients (src/app/admin/users/page.tsx:11-16, with the comment 'полноценный F-119-бан в карточке клиента = Sprint 3'). ClientHero has no ban/restrict action (only a copy button, src/app/admin/clients/[id]/ClientHero.tsx:140) and ModerationTab is read-only. There is no general 'restriction/limit' concept beyond permanent verification blocking-reject. Operationally, outside the verification blocking-reject path, an admin cannot ban or restrict an existing active user from the console at all.
gaps.fix_hint: Wire the existing F-119 ban dispatcher into the client card (propose/confirm/cancel UI for superadmin) and add a restrictions concept (temporary limits) with a Blocks screen listing active bans/restrictions, reasons, and audit.

gaps.title: No profile-content moderation queue/flow (Screen 6/7): profile text is not gated by admin approval before publish
gaps.detail: not_yet_built. Spec Screen 6 'Анкеты на модерации' (l.4553) and Screen 7 'Проверка анкеты' (l.5056) require a profile-content moderation queue with statuses (new/on-review/needs-changes/approved/rejected) so a profile does NOT enter Matching automatically ('Анкета не должна попадать в Matching автоматически', l.4571); Settings Screen 22 has a mandatory 'Модерация новых анкет — Требовать модерацию перед публикацией' toggle (l.16xxx). Built app has only identity verification (case studio) — there is NO profile-text moderation queue and no admin action to approve/reject/needs-changes profile content. ProfileTab (src/app/admin/clients/[id]/ProfileTab.tsx) is strictly read-only (no Button/onClick/fetch/approve/reject; only displays status/published_at at line 42,80). The sidebar has no 'Анкеты' section (src/components/admin-ops/OpsShell/OpsSidebar.tsx GROUPS). Operationally, the 'проверенные анкеты' promise for profile CONTENT (bio, goals, sensitive blocks) is not enforced by the admin — only identity is.
gaps.fix_hint: Add a profile_moderation status/queue; build a /admin/profiles review screen (or a moderation action in ProfileTab) with approve/needs-changes/reject and reason templates; gate profile publish→Matching on approval per Settings toggle.

gaps.title: Face-match step is a manual 3-checkbox attestation only — no similarity score / comparison field required by spec
gaps.detail: deviation (partial). Spec Screen 5 (l.4408) specifies a face_comparison payload with document_photo_url, selfie_photo_url, similarity_score (e.g. 98), result (high_similarity) and manual_review_required flag, plus a profile_comparison object comparing each document field against the profile value with match/mismatch status and overall_status. Built FaceMatchStep (src/components/admin-ops/case/FaceMatchStep.tsx) shows selfie + passport side-by-side with three manual checkboxes (face matches, liveness, age plausible) and no similarity score, no automated/assisted comparison, and no field-by-field document-vs-profile comparison table. This is a reasonable MVP substitution (manual attestation replaces automated scoring) but it is a documented deviation: there is no similarity_score stored/logged and no structured profile-comparison, so the spec's decision-support and later audit ('запуск сравнения фото') cannot be reconstructed.
gaps.fix_hint: Acceptable as MVP if intentional. To close: persist the moderator's face-match attestation (the 3 booleans) into case audit, and add a document-vs-profile field comparison view. If automated face-match is desired later, capture similarity_score + manual_review_required.

gaps.title: Audit log lacks sensitive-view events (document/selfie/PII viewed) that spec mandates; log is not immutable-verified
gaps.detail: partial. Spec Screen 5 (l.4408) and Screen 10 (l.7293) require logging of read/view actions on sensitive data: identity_detailed_card_opened, identity_document_viewed (sensitive_data:true), selfie viewed, risk-factors viewed, complaint_detail_opened, evidence_opened, related_chat_opened — each with reason. Built adminAudit (src/lib/admin/guard.ts:39) is only called on WRITE actions (login, ban_*, verification decisions, photo/report decisions). Viewing a passport in the case studio or a client's Identity/PII tab records NO audit entry (loadCase/loadClient sign URLs with no audit write; src/lib/admin/load-case.ts, load-client.ts). The out-of-queue scope-violation path IS logged (guard.ts recordScopeViolation) but legitimate in-scope PII views are not. Also the built log table (admin_audit_log) is a plain insert table with no hash-chain/immutability guarantee. Operationally, forensics cannot answer 'who viewed this user's passport' for in-scope accesses — a compliance gap the spec explicitly calls out (Legal, l.7360).
gaps.fix_hint: Emit audit events on sensitive-data views (document/selfie/PII-tab open) with reason capture; consider a reason prompt before revealing PII. Optionally add append-only/hash-chained audit for tamper-evidence.

gaps.title: Clients directory shows full PII to superadmin without masking/reason gate spec requires
gaps.detail: deviation. Spec Screen 2 (l.2446, l.2948) mandates that phone/Telegram/documents must be masked in list/directory views and revealed only with RBAC + reason + audit ('маскирование + RBAC + audit log'). Built clients directory is superadmin-only (OpsSidebar.tsx:44 superOnly), and the client card (src/app/admin/clients/[id]/page.tsx) gates moderators via checkInQueueOrSuperPage — but for a superadmin the full IdentityTab (ПИНФЛ, passport series/number, address; src/lib/admin/load-client.ts:70-107) and phone/Telegram render unmasked with no reason prompt and no view-audit. The reveal is coarse-grained (whole role) rather than the spec's per-field masking + reason + audit. This is defensible for a small superadmin set but deviates from the spec's data-minimization requirement and pairs with SG-09 (no view audit).
gaps.fix_hint: Mask phone/Telegram/passport by default in list and card; require an explicit 'reveal' with reason that writes an audit entry, per Screen 2/5. Tie reveal to a discrete permission rather than the whole superadmin role.

gaps.title: Operational modules entirely absent: Tariffs/Payments, Family, Individual, International, Matching status, Interests/Chats, Compatibility test, Notifications, System Settings
gaps.detail: not_yet_built. Spec defines 22 screens; the built admin implements ~ screens 1-11 partially (dashboard, verification/case studio, photos, reports list, clients directory/card, analytics, audit). Entirely missing with no page or API: Screen 12 Тарифы и платежи (l.8090), Screen 13 Family Add-on (l.8760), Screen 14 is Журнал (built), Screen 15 Matching status (l.10104), Screen 16 Интересы и чаты (l.10828), Screen 17 Individual подбор (l.11563), Screen 18 Международные пользователи (l.12320), Screen 19 Тест совместимости (l.13172), Screen 20 Уведомления (l.13956), Screen 22 Настройки системы (l.16006). Confirmed by grep: no international/family/individual/tariff/subscription/payment pages under src/app/admin. The dashboard even lacks the international-checks queue the spec calls a distinct queue (l.2245). These are large operational surfaces (e.g. International requires separate manual-review queue per l.2246; Settings holds the mandatory 'модерация новых анкет' and registration-mode toggles). Whether all are in-scope for MVP is a product call, but they are spec-required and currently unbuilt.
gaps.fix_hint: Prioritize by operational need. Near-term: System Settings (registration mode + profile-moderation toggle), International review queue, and Notifications. Tariffs/Family/Individual/Matching-status can follow as those product features ship.
